title: How a Brake Service Warranty Ends: Expiry, Supersession and Voiding
content:
**Condition 1 — Three ways a warranty ends.** A warranty under Brake Service Warranties ends in three ways, and the warranty must be in status active when it ends.

- **Expiry.** A limited warranty expires when its warranty months from the job's service date, or its warranty miles from the odometer on the job's repair order, is reached, whichever comes first. A lifetime warranty never expires on time or mileage. Expiry is applied by the system and records the date the limit was reached or recorded.
- **Supersession.** A warranty is superseded when a new paid job is done on the same axle, under the limit of one active warranty per axle. It is recorded on the date of the new job.
- **Voiding.** A warranty is voided when the purchaser no longer owns the vehicle — the warranty ends on vehicle sale and is not transferable — or when a lifetime line's vehicle enters commercial use under the commercial-use terms. It is recorded on the date recorded.

Supersession and voiding are recorded by a Crestline representative.

**Condition 2 — Statuses.** A warranty is active, expired, superseded or voided.

| Status before the event | May the warranty end now? |
|---|---|
| active | Yes, by expiry, supersession or voiding as above |
| expired, superseded or voided | No — the warranty must be active when it ends |

**Condition 3 — "Whichever comes first", illustrated.** Take an illustrative limited line of 6 months and 5000 miles, not any Crestline line's terms.

| Months since the job | Miles since the job | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 5000 reached | expired — the mile limit was reached first |
| 6 reached | 3000 | expired — the month limit was reached first |
| 4 | 3000 | neither limit reached; the warranty is not expired |

A lifetime warranty in the same positions never expires on time or mileage; it can still end by supersession or voiding.
